channel.title: Articles on History News — Where the Past Makes Headlines
channel.description: Recent content in Articles on History News — Where the Past Makes Headlines

item.title: The City That Burned
item.description: Using newly digitized photographs and survivor letters, this piece walks through the 7.9-magnitude earthquake and three-day fire that destroyed 80% of San Francisco in 1906.

item.title: Signed Into Shame
item.description: FDR’s Executive Order 9066, the internal memos debating its legality, and the decades-long fight for reparations.

item.title: The Zimmermann Telegram
item.description: How British intelligence decoded Germany’s secret proposal to Mexico, and why the UK waited weeks before revealing it to Washington.

item.title: The Night the Wall Came Down
item.description: The fall of the Berlin Wall told through ordinary citizens’ personal photos, diary entries, and amateur footage from across Europe.

item.title: How the Internet Broke on 9/11
item.description: Archived snapshots of CNN, BBC, and MSNBC from September 11, 2001 show how the nascent web struggled — and adapted — to cover the biggest story of its era.

item.title: Titanic Sunk
item.description: How rural American newspapers covered the Titanic disaster, from wildly inaccurate early reports to the grim corrections days later.

item.title: The Crime of the Century
item.description: A visual timeline of front-page coverage from 50+ newspapers tracking the kidnapping, ransom, discovery, and trial that consumed Depression-era America.

item.title: Killed by the King's Horse
item.description: How British papers — sympathetic and hostile — framed suffragette Emily Davison’s death at the 1913 Epsom Derby.

item.title: One Giant Headline
item.description: A survey of international newspaper front pages from July 21, 1969 — from celebration to grudging acknowledgment behind the Iron Curtain.

item.title: Mask Up or Shut Down
item.description: Public health journals from 1918-1920 reveal how cities that acted early survived the Spanish Flu better than those that didn’t.

item.title: The Book That Changed Everything
item.description: A guided reading of key passages from Darwin’s Origin of Species, showing how radical and carefully diplomatic his arguments were.

item.title: Locked Doors and Broken Ladders
item.description: The original investigation transcripts and coroner reports reconstruct the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire that killed 146 garment workers.

item.title: Would You Flip the Switch?
item.description: Stanley Milgram’s original papers reveal how easily ordinary people can be pushed to inflict harm when told to by an authority figure.

item.title: 12 Seconds That Changed the World
item.description: High-resolution images of the original Wright Flyer, the brothers’ notebooks, and their telegram home reconstruct the birth of aviation.

item.title: Declassified Disaster
item.description: Declassified internal assessments reveal the agency’s own analysts warned the invasion would fail — and were overruled by political pressure.

item.title: Justice at Nuremberg
item.description: An analysis of the Nuremberg Charter and key trial transcripts that established the precedent that ‘following orders’ is not a legal defense.

item.title: Voices from Omaha Beach
item.description: First-person accounts from soldiers, medics, and French civilians paint an intimate portrait of the Normandy invasion.

item.title: The Most Reproduced Photo in History
item.description: The full story behind Joe Rosenthal’s iconic Iwo Jima photograph — including the lesser-known first flag raising and the men’s fates.

item.title: Dealey Plaza in Focus
item.description: The press photographers in the motorcade, the amateur films, and how visual evidence shaped the JFK investigation.

item.title: London Burned for Four Days
item.description: How the Great Fire destroyed medieval London yet led to modern building codes, fire insurance, and Christopher Wren’s reimagined city.

item.title: I Shall Resign
item.description: A close reading of Nixon’s televised resignation speech — what he said, what he didn’t say, and how the nation reacted.

item.title: The Shot That Started a World War
item.description: How a wrong turn by a driver put Archduke Franz Ferdinand’s car directly in front of his assassin in Sarajevo.

item.title: Wonderful Things
item.description: Howard Carter’s dramatic discovery of Tutankhamun’s tomb and the media frenzy that launched global Egyptomania.

item.title: 26 Seconds to Meltdown
item.description: A clear explanation of what went wrong at Chernobyl’s Reactor No. 4, why the design was flawed, and how the Soviet cover-up unraveled.

item.title: The Day the Revolution Began
item.description: Contemporary illustrations, maps, and eyewitness accounts reconstruct the hours-long siege that became the symbol of the French Revolution.
